about: SysML v2 draws about a dozen kinds of diagram from one notation vocabulary. Several look alike at a glance: a parts tree and an interconnection view differ only by port squares and connectors; a definition view and a parts tree share the same rectangles but not the same corners. These cards describe what each kind looks like well enough for a vision model to classify it and read it, without the model text. Every card names a figure from the OMG SysML v2 reference implementation and states whether it was checked against that figure at 1200 px with zoomed crops, or written from the view taxonomy and not yet verified.
decision_tree:
1. Is there an enclosing frame? Read the frame's header. A tab with a clipped corner carrying `«view» Name : Some View` is a rendered view whose *contents* are whatever the view renders (fig-68 is a state machine inside a «view» tab; fig-72's frames are plain bold names). A frame whose header is just `«part» name : Type` or `«action» name : Type` is an interconnection or action flow of that element.
2. No frame? Then classify by marks, in this order:
   - small hollow squares straddling box borders, with names written outside the box → interconnection view (ports).
   - no squares, and every line has a small filled diamond at one box and nothing at the other → parts tree (or a variability tree if `«variation»`/`«variant»` appear).
   - boxes with `«part def»`/`«attribute def»` keyword lines, square corners → definition view.
   - thick dark bars splitting one flow, plus a `start`/`^done` pair → action flow.
   - a `«requirement»` tree with `<1>`, `<2>` ids and italic `doc`/`attributes`/`constraints` compartments → requirement view.
   - `«individual occurrence»`, `«snapshot occurrence»`, `«timeslice occurrence»` → object/instance view.
   - bold single-line names in plain boxes with hollow triangles up the page and dense `+/role  0..*  {subsets ...}` labels → abstract-syntax (metamodel) diagram, not a user diagram.
3. Text settles the rest: `part def` vs `part`, `:>` subset vs `:>>` redefine vs `=` bind, `[1..4]` multiplicity, `«satisfy»`/`«verify»`/`«require»`/`«perform»`/`«expose»`/`«import»` on dashed arrows.
reading_order: Classify first (decision tree). Then: frame header → keyword line inside each box → box title and `: Type` → compartment titles → which end of each edge carries the diamond, triangle or arrow → edge labels and guards → `id =` / `text =` rows. Never infer direction from label placement; read the end marks. When two boxes share a name, the one with `def` in its keyword is the definition.

marks.mark: small filled black diamond at one end
marks.means: composition — that end owns the other. In a parts tree the diamond is at the PARENT.
marks.gotcha: on diagonal lines the rotated diamond reads as a small black square

marks.means: in the reference figures this appears on `«subject»` membership (fig-70) and on some part decompositions (fig-72)
marks.gotcha: the corpus is inconsistent here — do not infer ownership kind from hollow-vs-filled alone; read the keyword lines

marks.mark: hollow triangle pointing at a box
marks.means: specialisation; the pointed-at box is the general type
marks.gotcha: several subclasses may share ONE triangle on a bus line (fig-24) — do not expect one per edge

marks.means: reference, satisfy, require, perform, expose, import — the label says which
marks.gotcha: plain connectors between ports in an interconnection view have NO arrowheads at all
action flow edges are dashed in fig-67 and solid in fig-66

marks.mark: small chevron `>` or `←` inside a port square
marks.gotcha: the chevron, not the arrowhead, gives direction when the connector has no arrowhead

marks.mark: thick dark bar across a flow
marks.means: fork or join — several flows split from, or merge into, this point
marks.gotcha: two bars stacked close together are two separate forks

marks.mark: small `*` beside a box or line
marks.means: membership/ownership marker in requirement and decomposition figures
marks.gotcha: easy to mistake for a footnote or multiplication sign

marks.mark: grey box, grey text, no bold
marks.means: a class from another package or an abstract class in abstract-syntax figures
marks.gotcha: in diagrams proper, grey is only used for `«keyword»` lines

coverage: Verified against reference figures: definition/usage, parts tree, interconnection, action flow, state transition, requirement, verification case, view and rendering, variability, individuals/snapshots, abstract syntax. Written from the view taxonomy but NOT yet checked against a figure: package/namespace, use case, constraint/assert. Not covered at all: tabular and relationship-matrix views, sequence views (no reference figure inspected).

views.purpose: Declares types (definitions) and the roles that use them (usages). A definition names a kind of thing and its features; a usage says a thing of that kind exists in a context, possibly redefining values.
identify_by: keyword line inside each box: «part def», «attribute def», «item def», … for definitions; «part», «attribute», «item», … for usages
a definition's box has SQUARE corners, a usage's box has ROUNDED corners — the single most reliable visual tell in the reference figures
a usage's header reads `name : Type`; a definition's header reads only the name
compartment titles are bare nouns on definitions (`attributes`, `parts`, `ports`, `actions`) and verb+noun on usages (`perform actions`, `exhibit states`)

nodes.shape: rectangle, square corners, keyword + centred name, rule-separated compartments
nodes.text: «part def» / Vehicle / attributes `mass :> mass` / ports `ignitionCmdPort : IgnitionCmdPort`

nodes.shape: rectangle, ROUNDED corners, keyword + `name : Type`, then compartments
small square on a box border

edges.ends: filled diamond at the whole end
edges.label: multiplicity at the whole end, e.g. `1`

edges.ends: hollow triangle at the parent
open arrow
open arrow labelled «satisfy»/«derive»/«verify»

confuse_with.how_to_tell: a parts tree has only rounded usage boxes and only composition edges; here square definition boxes sit among the rounded ones
interconnection views add port squares on borders and connect square-to-square

views.notes: Row grammar carries meaning: `:>` subsets, `:>>` redefines (italic row), `=` binds, `default` value, `[n..m]` multiplicity; `perform`/`exhibit` are bold at the start of action/state rows.

views.sysml_v2_view: GeneralView restricted to composition of usages
views.purpose: Whole–part decomposition of one part: the root box is the whole, every other box is a part it owns, and nesting shows sub-parts.

frame.header: unframed; the root box is not marked differently from the rest

identify_by: every box has the same rounded shape and the same «part» keyword — no definition boxes at all
every edge is a composition: small filled diamond at the parent, nothing at the child
no ports, no arrowheads, no guards; very wide and shallow (one band of boxes per ownership level)
`name : Type` on every box; a box that owns sub-parts may omit the `: Type`

nodes.shape: rounded rectangle, «part» italic above, `name : Type` below, thin rule and empty strip

nodes.means: a part that itself has parts

edges.style: solid straight, fanned radially from the parent's corners
edges.ends: filled diamond at the parent, plain at the child
edges.means: ownership; read the diamond to find the parent
edges.label: multiplicity on the child end when it is not 1, e.g. `2`

confuse_with.how_to_tell: no square-cornered definition boxes here, and no non-composition edges
no port squares and no connectors between siblings
if boxes carry «variation» or «variant» it is a variability tree

views.notes: Diamonds from adjacent children can overlap into a dark blob at the parent's edge — count them by following each line, not by counting blobs.

views.purpose: The internal structure of one part: its parts shown inside the owner's frame, wired port to port.

frame.header: rounded frame, header band with «part» over `name : Vehicle` (bold, spaces around the colon)

identify_by: one frame around everything, headed by the owner part
boxes nested inside boxes to show ownership
small hollow squares straddling box borders with the port name printed OUTSIDE the box
connectors run port-to-port and have NO arrowheads; direction, where shown, is a tiny chevron inside the port square

nodes.shape: rounded rectangle inside the frame, «part» over bold name, optional italic `attributes` compartment
hollow small square straddling a border, name outside
port square on the frame border itself
nodes.means: a port of the owner, exposed at its boundary

edges.ends: none (no arrowheads)
edges.label: sometimes a bare `=` glyph above the line; no guards, no multiplicities

confuse_with.how_to_tell: ports and port-to-port wiring are present here and absent there; here boxes nest inside a frame
action flows have arrowheads and often dashed lines; interconnection connectors have none

views.notes: A three-line stack of squares on the frame's left border (two `wheelToRoadPort` squares plus one `vehicleToRoadPort` label) reads as a single label until zoomed.

views.purpose: How actions consume and produce items and control: a flow from inputs through actions to outputs, with forks and joins.

frame.header: rounded frame titled «action» over `name : Type`, or «use case» over the use-case name when the flow belongs to a use case

identify_by: «action» boxes with `name : Type` and no pins inside
ports as squares with a small chevron for direction; labels sit outside the box, split over two lines (`engineTorque :` / `Torque`)
thick dark horizontal bars where one flow becomes several, or several become one
`start` and `^done` as rounded «use case» boxes (not the UML filled circle / bullseye)
one swallowtail (right edge pulled inward to a point) box for `«accept action»`

nodes.shape: rounded rectangle, «action», stacked name and bold type
rectangle with a concave right edge (swallowtail)
nodes.means: accept action — waits for a signal
fork (one in, many out) or join (many in, one out)

edges.style: dashed in fig-67, solid in fig-66
edges.ends: small filled triangle at the target
edges.label: none, or a guard where the flow is conditional

edges.ends: no arrowhead; direction from the port chevron
edges.label: item name and `[mult]` on the port label, e.g. `vehicleToRoadTorque [2] :` / `Torque`

confuse_with.how_to_tell: states are boxes with entry/do/exit compartments and edges carrying `[guard]`/`when`; actions here have no such compartments
arrowheads and bars here; connectors without arrowheads there

views.notes: In fig-67 every box says `«use case»` or `«action»` while the frame says `«use case»` — the frame keyword describes the owning behaviour, not the boxes.

views.purpose: The lifecycle of one exhibited state: its regions, states, entry/do/exit behaviour, guards and transitions.

frame.header: tab with clipped corner: «view» `Name : State Transition View`

identify_by: one big rounded region per concurrent sub-machine, each with its own small filled initial dot
state boxes with italic `actions` compartment holding bold `entry` / `do` / `exit` lines
edges labelled with `trigger [guard] / effect`, where `send` and `when` appear in bold
`«exhibit state»` above the region name, with bold `parallel` when regions run concurrently

nodes.shape: large rounded region labelled with the substate name
rounded box with a `ref parts` compartment

edges.ends: small OPEN V arrowhead
edges.label: `iCmd : IgnitionCmd [iCmd.ignitionOnOff == on]` / `send StartSignal to Controller`

confuse_with.how_to_tell: state boxes carry entry/do/exit; action boxes carry ports and item labels instead
states are rounded and grouped in regions; definitions are not

views.notes: Guard text can be truncated at the figure edge; quote what is legible and flag the missing `]` rather than inventing it.

views.purpose: A tree of requirements with their subject, documentation, values and assumptions.
identify_by: boxes headed «requirement» with a number in angle brackets: `<1> vehicleMassRequirement : MassRequirement`
italic compartment titles `doc`, `attributes`, `constraints`, `subject`, `references`
`doc` holds prose; `attributes` mixes `x = 2000 [kg]` with `:>>Type::x` redefinition rows
bold `assume` inside a `constraints` compartment, holding `{...}`
composition edges to child requirements carry a small `*` near the child

nodes.shape: rounded rectangle, «requirement», `<n> name : Type`, ruled compartments

nodes.means: the thing the requirement is about

edges.ends: filled diamond at the parent requirement, plain at the child
edges.label: `*` beside the child

edges.ends: hollow diamond at the requirement end
open arrow labelled «satisfy»/«verify»/«derive»
edges.means: cross-cutting relationship between requirements or to a design element

confuse_with.how_to_tell: verification figures add «verification»/«verification def» boxes and «perform»/«objective»/«require» arrows

views.notes: This figure is the counter-example to 'hollow diamond = subject everywhere': here it does, and hollow-vs-filled is the only visual difference between requirement ownership and subject membership.

views.purpose: How a verification case is performed: the system of parts and actions that run the test, the objective, and the requirement it verifies.

frame.header: several plain tabbed frames with BOLD roman headers and no guillemets, e.g. `VerificationSystem`, `VerificationCases1`, `VerificationCaseDefinitions`

identify_by: multiple tabbed frames arranged side by side, headers bold with no «»
«verification» box with a `: TestType` and a `metadata` compartment
«verification def» boxes with square corners and large roman names
bold guillemet edge labels «perform», «objective», «require»

nodes.shape: square-cornered box, «verification def» over a large name

edges.ends: hollow diamond at the owner end
edges.means: part decomposition in the performing system

edges.ends: filled diamond at the case end
open arrow labelled «perform»
open arrow labelled «objective» or «require»
hollow triangle at the general case definition

confuse_with.how_to_tell: requirement figures show only requirement boxes; this one adds the performing system and actions
case frames have bold plain headers; interconnection frames are headed «part» name : Type

views.notes: Both hollow and filled diamonds appear in this single figure for what look like the same relationship; trust the keyword lines over the diamond style.

views.purpose: Declares concerns, viewpoints and view definitions, and shows which view exposes or imports what; a rendering is the picture a view produces.

frame.header: several floating tabbed frames with BOLD roman headers (`ViewpointDefinitions`, `VehicleSafetyView`, `ViewDefinitions`, `PartsTree`) — no guillemets

identify_by: `«concern def»`, `«viewpoint def»`, `«view def»`, `«view»` keywords
dashed edges labelled «import»*, «satisfy», «expose»* — the asterisk is superscript and easy to miss
solid edges ending in hollow triangles between view definitions (specialisation)
a rendering figure that is JUST the tagged boxes the view selected — no frame, no arrows, `«#Safety»`-style tags over part names

nodes.means: a concern and who cares about it
nodes.text: «concern def» / `VehicleSafety` / doc 'identify system safety features' / stakeholders `se: SafetyEngineer`

nodes.shape: box «viewpoint def» with italic `concerns` holding bold `require`

nodes.means: a view definition; may hold a `renderings` compartment

nodes.shape: rounded box «#Safety» over a bare name, empty lower compartment
nodes.means: a rendering: the elements the view selected

edges.ends: small filled arrowhead
edges.means: «import»* or «expose»* between view, viewpoint and rendering

edges.ends: small filled arrowhead
edges.means: «satisfy» from a view to a viewpoint

edges.ends: hollow triangle at the general view definition

confuse_with.how_to_tell: the keywords are about views and concerns, and the edges are dashed with «import»/«expose»
a rendering may look like a parts tree with no edges at all; it has tags over names and no diamonds

views.notes: Dashed runs may share one horizontal and read as a T-junction; follow each label to its arrowhead instead of assuming one edge.

views.purpose: Which parts of a family are variable, which alternatives exist, and what selects among them.
identify_by: boxes carrying BOTH `«variation»` and `«part»`, and boxes carrying BOTH `«variant»` and `«part»`
small circles hanging off a variation box's bottom edge: ⊗ (circle with ×) and ⊕ (circle with +) selecting alternatives
one large `«assert constraint»` box holding an `xor` expression over the alternatives
the usual composition diamonds from the family box to each part, with italic multiplicity `1`

nodes.shape: rounded box, two keyword lines «variation» «part», `name : Type`
small circle with ×, small circle with +

edges.ends: filled diamond at the family end, plain at the part
edges.label: `1` at part ends

edges.ends: filled diamond above a large hollow triangle
edges.label: `6` for a six-cylinder part

confuse_with.how_to_tell: «variation»/«variant» keywords and the constraint box are present only here

views.notes: The ⊗/⊕ circles are the only 'port-like' marks on these boxes; do not report them as ports.

views.purpose: A concrete instance over time: one individual, its time slice, and per-time snapshots of its parts.
identify_by: keywords «individual occurrence», «timeslice occurrence», «snapshot occurrence»
names of the form `t0_a`, `t0_r: Road_1` — instance names with types
strict column repeat, one column per snapshot time, each column the same shape
small filled diamond at the container end of every line, rotated to lie along diagonal lines

nodes.shape: rounded box, «snapshot occurrence», with `attributes` holding `tN =N [s]` and `:>>Context::time`

edges.ends: filled diamond at the container end, none at the child
edges.label: none

confuse_with.how_to_tell: instance names with `_1`/`_2` suffixes and snapshot keywords; parts trees use definition types
no definitions here at all

views.notes: Diamonds on 45° lines read as black squares; that is one marker rotated, not two different markers.

views.sysml_v2_view: not a user view — a specification figure
views.purpose: Defines the language itself: classes, their specialisations and their associations. Appears in the specification, not in models you are asked to read.
identify_by: plain square-cornered boxes with BOLD single-word names and no keyword lines, no compartments
vertical ladders joined by hollow triangles (specialisation)
association labels of the form `+/role  0..*  {subsets feature}` — role name, multiplicity, constraint
greyed boxes with grey text among black ones
one hollow triangle may serve several subclasses on a shared bus line

nodes.shape: grey-filled box with grey bold name
nodes.means: class from another package or abstract class

edges.ends: large hollow triangle at the general class
small solid dot at the owning class plus a tiny open arrow at the target
edges.label: `+/source 1`, `+/effectAction 0..* {subsets feature}`

confuse_with.how_to_tell: no «keyword» lines, no compartments, and the role labels use `+/` and `{subsets ...}`

views.notes: If a figure looks like a family tree of types with dense role labels on both sides of every line, it is the specification defining the language, not a model of a system.

views.purpose: How the model is organised: packages, their members and the imports between them.

identify_by: folded-corner or tabbed rectangles holding other boxes
dashed arrows labelled «import» between packages
member boxes inside, often the definitions themselves

edges.ends: open arrow

confuse_with.how_to_tell: view frames carry «view»/«viewpoint def» keywords and «expose»/«satisfy» labels

views.notes: Described from the view taxonomy; not yet checked against a rendered figure.

actor boxes or stick figures at the boundary
dashed arrows labelled «include» / «extends» between use cases

edges.ends: open arrow labelled «include»/«extends»

views.purpose: Mathematical or logical constraints on the model, and the assertions that hold at a point in behaviour.
identify_by: boxes headed «constraint def» / «constraint» / «calc def» / «assert constraint»
compartments titled `parameters` or `operator expressions` holding expressions
binding edges labelled `=` between parameters and the values they bind

edges.ends: none
edges.means: binding of a parameter to a value, labelled `=`
